items.title: fix(workflow): reserve lane-header clearance for inferred vertical straight routes (#565)
items.body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

Fixes #565.

In `archify/renderers/workflow/workflow-compiler.mjs`, column shift calculation for lane headers (`laneHeaderShift`) collected endpoints entering the top of a lane using `unpinnedTopEndpointIds`. However, it previously only checked explicit authored sides (`edge.fromSide === 'top'` or `edge.toSide === 'top'`).

For vertical straight routes (`route: "straight"`) connecting two nodes in the same column across adjacent lanes without explicit endpoint sides, the compiler inferred `bottom -> top` (or `top -> bottom`), but because the top endpoint was not registered in `unpinnedTopEndpointIds`, the column position was not shifted rightward to clear the lane header text. Consequently, the vertical route collided with the lane header and failed validation with `workflow/route-preset-conflict`, while adding an explicit `toSide: "top"` passed cleanly.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: Low (bounded workflow readable-v2 layout clearance for same-column vertical straight routes).
- Changed behavior: When an edge declares `route: "straight"` without explicit side pins between nodes in the same column across different lanes, the inferred top endpoint is included in `unpinnedTopEndpointIds` so that the column is shifted to clear the lane header text.
- Preserved behavior:
  - Authored side annotations remain fully authoritative.
  - Non-straight or horizontal edges, edges with horizontal pins (`channelX` or `via`), and outside routes remain unaffected.
  - All existing workflow compiler test baselines and hard contract suites pass without change.

## Tests run

- Evaluated head `6005435` against base `upstream/main` (`d5a1333`).
- `node --test archify/test/workflow-compiler.test.mjs`: All 43 tests pass (42 existing + 1 new regression test verifying that inferred top endpoints reserve lane-header clearance for both downward and upward vertical straight routes).
- `node --test archify/test/workflow-compiler-hard-contract.test.mjs`: All 76 tests pass.
- `node --test archify/test/layout-rules.test.mjs`: All 125 tests pass.
- Minimal reproduction CLI verification: `node archify/bin/archify.mjs validate workflow <repro.json> --quality showcase --json` passes with `status: "pass"` and `maxBends: 0`.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify.zip`: Rebuilt with canonical Node 22 (`v22.23.3`, bundled zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`) via `scripts/build-zip.sh`.

SHA-256: `bae16dded8b957030d5235543e20943eec3f842a1a76af90864b152ca60ed3ac`. Relative to current dev, only Sequence README, Sequence renderer and Sequence width checker entries change. - **Final-head CI:** passed on this exact head (all executed jobs succeeded; `deploy-pages` was intentionally skipped). [run 37791783128](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/37791783128). ## Merge Danger — scope and compatibility **Door:** two-way (reversible code change). **Blast Radius:** Sequence. Schema and authored `y`/`viewBox` remain authoritative. `standard` preserves acceptance; `showcase` intentionally rejects newly detected note/segment collisions with `sequence/note-overlap`, `sequence/note-canvas-limit` and `sequence/segment-label-overlap` diagnostics. No release or live installation update is included. --- ## Historical author implementation and evidence The sections below retain the author's original revision-specific evidence and screenshots. They are not new runs on the synchronized head; the current maintainer verification is recorded above. Fixes #676. ## Problem and value On the current base (`dev` @ 7a3e1f3), a sequence `messages[].note` is drawn as a single unmeasured `` line. A long note runs past its arrow, through activation bars and into neighbouring lanes, while `validate`, `deliver`, `check` and `browser-check` all pass. Notes are fine-detail text, visible only at ≥175% zoom, so the overflow is easy to miss. Following the direction agreed in #676 (wrap within the message span; keep the full text in the Viewer and in image exports; no silent truncation): - A note wraps inside one gap between neighbouring lifelines: the widest gap the message spans, nearest the sender on a tie, so it never crosses an unrelated lifeline or activation bar. It keeps 11px from each lifeline (5px activation half-width + 6px). - Long unbroken text (URLs, paths) breaks after `/ . - ? & = # _` where possible, otherwise at any grapheme. Every character stays visible, including in PNG/JPEG exports. - Wrapping follows the existing dataflow stage-header pattern (`` lines, line height = font + 4, grapheme-safe splitting). - If a wrapped note still reaches a later message (its arrow, label or note), `showcase` validation fails with an actionable diagnostic instead of moving authored `y` values, e.g.: `Note on message "forward" wraps to 2 lines (down to y=265) and reaches message "ack" at y=262 — move "ack" and later messages down so it sits at y=287 or below, or shorten the note.` ## Stability impact - **Impact class:** contract change (new `showcase` validation failure for a note that reaches a later message, scope agreed in #676) plus local Sequence renderer behavior. Changed: `renderers/sequence/render-sequence.mjs`; the Sequence-only width review in `scripts/check-render-output.mjs` (`collectSequenceColumnSpace`). - **Preserved:** a note that fits on one line keeps its exact original markup and position (`x` = arrow start + 12, `y` = message y + 18). Authored `y` values and `viewBox` are never changed. Schema unchanged; existing schema-v1 JSON stays valid. `standard` gets no new failure, so existing standard diagrams keep rendering. No shipped example uses `note`. - **Intended changes:** - Wrapped notes render as several `` lines. - The automatic canvas height counts the wrapped note height, so a tall note on the last message stays above the legend. - The Sequence width review now measures `` lines instead of returning `measured: false`. - One existing test expectation changed (`sequence-width-review.test.mjs`): it relied on a long CJK note spilling into the blank right-hand area. The note now stays in its lane, so that area is genuinely empty and `reviewSuggested` is correctly `true`. The test is split: the label half is unchanged, and the note half asserts the new behavior. - **Failure behavior:** `showcase` only, reported as a `layout/constraint` diagnostic naming the blocking message and the minimum `y` it needs. ## Tests run Comparison base `dev` @ 7a3e1f3a (where the change was written and the full suite compared); candidate `fix/sequence-note-wrap` @ bfbb02b9, then merged with `dev` @ 078c583a as c04b385a (test moved to the relocated top-level `test/`). The focused tests below were rerun on c04b385a. Windows 11, Node 22.18.0. - New `test/sequence-note-wrap.test.mjs` (8 tests, all pass): reported case wraps and keeps every word; URL breaks after punctuation and keeps every character; no-punctuation token breaks at characters; short note markup unchanged; skip-over messages use the gap beside the sender (both directions); crowded note fails with the exact `y`, and applying that `y` passes; `standard` still accepts a crowded note; automatic canvas grows for a wrapped late note. - `node --test test/sequence-width-review.test.mjs test/edge-label-color.test.mjs test/layout-rules.test.mjs test/sequence-column-fit.test.mjs test/geometry.test.mjs`: pass. - Full `npm test` on base and candidate on the same Windows machine: failure lists are identical (Windows-only symlink EPERM, 8.3 short-path `QADRIL~1` vs long-path comparisons, cache/lock races), apart from `a killed checker holding the cache claim can be followed by a new check` (`delivery-update.test.mjs`), which failed once on the candidate and passed 3/3 on rerun. No Sequence test fails. I'll rely on CI for the Linux/macOS runs. ## Visual evidence - **Evidence provided:** matched before/after captures for the three cases requested in #676: the reported case, long unbroken text, and closely spaced messages. For the crowded case, *before* shows the note running under the next label; *after* shows the diagnostic, and then the same diagram with the suggested `y` applied. Each image shows the same input before (top) and after (bottom), cropped to the notes. **1. Reported case** **2. Long unbroken text** **3. Closely spaced: the note reaches the next message.** The candidate fails `validate` with the diagnostic above; the bottom capture applies the suggested `y=287`. **4. Closely spaced: the note fits** - **Comparison conditions:** same input JSON per row, `showcase`, `column_fit: "spread"`, headless Chrome 1440×900 at device scale 2, dark theme, Classic preset, still motion. Captures use the `full` detail level (what ≥175% zoom shows), set via `data-detail-level="full"` on the diagram container so notes are visible. - **Automated or browser checks:** every *after* case passes `finalize --quality showcase` (validate, deliver, check, browser-check). The crowded input fails `validate` with the diagnostic above; with the suggested `y` it passes all four gates. - **Perceptual visual review:** passed (author review of the captures). One thing worth your eyes: in the "closely spaced (fits)" case, the note "miss after 5 minutes" sits close to the neighbouring `query` label. It doesn't overlap, but feedback on that spacing is welcome. ## Generated artifacts None regenerated. No shipped Sequence example or gallery source uses `note`, and the golden check passes unchanged.

items.title: feat(code analyzers): M1: add extract step producing raw-facts.json
items.body: ## Problem and value Archify renders and validates typed JSON IR but deliberately performs no code analysis of its own; the agent authoring the IR is the only source of "what does this repository look like". This PR starts an `analyzers/` subsystem (design: `analyzers/ARCHITECTURE.md`, v0.2) that produces deterministic, evidence-backed facts about a repository, so architecture IR — and later coupling/redundancy findings — can be derived from source instead of from an agent's reading of it. Maintainer-approved scope: the isolated M1 extraction step; graph generation and PR impact analysis remain follow-up work. ## Scope - What changed: - New `analyzers/` package (private, Node ≥18, devDeps: `typescript`, `ajv`). - `analyzers/bin/analyze.mjs` with one command: `extract [--out] [--config] [--language] [--json]`. - TypeScript Compiler API adapter (`extract/ts/`, `allowJs`) extracting files, file roles (`source | test | generated`, precedence test > generated > source), and import edges (`static | dynamic | require | export`) with line numbers, imported names, and in-tree resolution via `ts.resolveModuleName`. Unresolved specifiers are kept and counted as `external | outside | unknown` so misses stay visible. - `analyzers/schemas/raw-facts.schema.json` (draft 2020-12); output is validated before write, arrays are stably sorted, no timestamps. - Failures are structured diagnostics (`code / severity / subject / evidence / supportedFixes`) mirroring `archify/renderers/shared/diagnostics.mjs`; `--json` never prints a Node stack. - Tests: synthetic fixture with hand-written `expected.json`; structured-failure test; self-bootstrap against `archify/` (schema pass, byte-for-byte determinism across two runs, hand-verified import list for `renderers/shared/validator.mjs`, dynamic-import edges from `bin/archify.mjs`, role assertions). - Root `.gitignore`: `out/` added for analyzer output. - What deliberately did not change: nothing under `archify/` — no renderer, schema, validator, viewer, CLI, dependency, generated artifact, or `archify.zip` change. `symbols` and `calls` exist in the schema but are empty (reserved for M2). - No unrelated changes: confirmed; the diff is `analyzers/**`, one `.gitignore` line, and the isolated analyzer CI job. ## Stability impact - Compatibility and migration risk: none for existing users; `analyzers/` is a separate package, not part of the installed skill, not referenced by `archify/package.json`, and now covered by an independent analyzers CI job. - Renderer, validator, package, or generated-artifact risk: none; `archify/` bytes are untouched. - Failure behavior and rollback path: every failure exits 1 with a structured diagnostic and writes no output file. Rollback is deleting `analyzers/` and the one `.gitignore` line. ## Tests run **CI:** `analyzers` job added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in 4ecbe9e (by @tt-a1i). Run on this head: <[link](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/34204331530/job/101990309501?pr=352)> ``` cd analyzers; npm test (Windows 11, Node v24.19.0) ok 1 - extract: synthetic fixture yields the expected files, imports, and unresolved counts ok 2 - extract: failures are structured diagnostics, never stacks ok 3 - extract: archify/ self-bootstrap passes schema and is byte-for-byte deterministic ok 4 - extract: hand-verified import lists for two archify files # tests 4 # pass 4 # fail 0 node analyzers/bin/analyze.mjs extract ./archify --out out/raw-facts.json --json { "status": "ok", "adapter": "ts", "files": 137, "imports": 849, "resolved": 132, "unresolved": { "external": 713, "outside": 4, "unknown": 0 } } 137 files = 35 source / 100 test / 2 generated. The 4 "outside" edges are test imports of ../../scripts/*.mjs. Two consecutive runs produced identical bytes (asserted by test 3). cd archify; npm ci; npm test (Windows 11, Node v24.19.0, Git 2.55.0.windows.3, Developer Mode on) 1051 tests: 1001 pass / 10 fail / 40 skipped ``` All 10 `archify/` failures are pre-existing Windows-only issues in upstream tests; none touch `analyzers/`, and this PR changes nothing under `archify/`. Upstream CI runs on ubuntu-latest only. - Unix assumptions in tests (6): `checkout-line-endings` ×3 (`/dev/null` → `\\.\nul`), `clean-skill-staging:90` (POSIX mode bits 0o755 vs 0o666), `readme-showcase:264` (Windows path passed to `/bin/bash`), `workflow-migration:452` (absolute path passed to `import()` without `file://` → `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME`). - Missing tool / version (2): `cursor-onboarding:41` (no `unzip`), `release-package-gates:527` (canonical `archify.zip` requires Node 22). - Process/timing (2): `cli:454` (preview exits via SIGTERM on Windows), `update-notifier:1951` (`silent` vs `update_available`; not yet classified). An initial run showed 43 failures; putting Git on PATH for the Node process and enabling Windows Developer Mode (symlink creation) reduced them to these 10. ## Visual evidence Not applicable — this change adds a CLI that emits JSON and touches no rendered output. Reproducible check: `node analyzers/bin/analyze.mjs extract ./archify --json` and compare with the numbers above. - Evidence provided: command output above; `analyzers/test/fixtures/ts-basic/expected.json` documents the exact expected extraction for the synthetic fixture. - Comparison conditions, when applicable: Not applicable. - Automated or browser checks: `analyzers` unit tests (4/4). - Perceptual visual review: Not applicable ## Generated artifacts None regenerated. Gallery, guides, README proofs, and `archify.zip` remain fresh because no source under `archify/` or `docs/` changed. ## Checklist - [x] I used a minimal focused change and preserved existing typed JSON behavior unless the issue requires a contract change. - [x] I ran the relevant targeted tests and `npm test` in `archify/`. - [x] I added or updated a regression test for behavioral changes. - [x] I checked generated artifacts and package freshness when their sources changed. - [x] I removed secrets, private repository content, and customer data from fixtures and screenshots. Failures are coming from Unix tests; Windows doesn't have the executable bit ## Maintainer repair validation Candidate `2fbceb8265551a34aa7dbe0a2f50ccee143cdfad` fixes import-equals extraction, shadowed require false edges, unmatched-glob hangs, directory-alias provenance, and locale-dependent ordering. An independent analyzer CI job installs and tests this package. Local validation: macOS, Node 22, `cd analyzers && npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm test`: 8 passed, 0 failed. Regressions exercise the CLI for import bindings, invalid config/no output, and cross-locale byte equality; Git provenance covers directory aliases and subdirectories. Existing self-bootstrap and golden facts still pass. Supported require handling is conservative: native unbound CommonJS require and a named (including aliased) Node createRequire import initialized with import.meta.url. Arbitrary loader factories and other createRequire bases are not inferred as dependency edges. No renderer or packaged artifact was modified by these repairs.

items.title: feat(import): add Mermaid flowchart importer for typed architecture IR
items.body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

Archify could not import existing Mermaid `flowchart` / `graph` diagrams. Users had to re-author topology by hand even when a Mermaid source already existed. Issue #92 asks for an end-to-end import path that maps a documented subset to typed Archify architecture IR, validates it through the existing gates, and delivers it as a standalone artifact.

## Scope

- New `archify/importers/flowchart.mjs` — focused Mermaid flowchart parser mapping a documented subset of `flowchart` / `graph` syntax to typed architecture IR. Supported: direction declarations (`TB`/`TD`, `BT`, `LR`, `RL`), node shapes (`[...]`, `(...)`, `((...))`, `[(...)]`, `{...}`, `>...]`), directed edges (`-->`, `-.->`, `==>`, `-- text -->`, `-. Text .->`, `|label|`), subgraphs, comments, and chained edges. Node text, edge labels, subgraph grouping, mirrored `RL`/`BT` placement, nested subgraph membership, and long-label canvas containment are preserved.
- New `archify import flowchart <input.mmd> [output.json] [--json]` CLI command.
- `test/flowchart-import.test.mjs` regression suite covering valid, malformed, unsupported, adversarial, showcase-layout, blank-label, XML-disallowed-character, and long-label canvas-containment fixtures (relocated with upstream's `archify/test` → `test/` move).
- Fixture files under `test/fixtures/flowchart/`.
- `archify/references/mermaid-flowchart-import.md` documenting the supported subset, shape/edge mapping, blank-label behavior, XML-character restrictions, nested-subgraph membership, and the diagnostic-code table; linked from `archify/SKILL.md` § Mermaid input.
- No schema, renderer, validator, or existing CLI command was modified.

## Stability impact

- Compatibility and migration risk: None. The importer is purely additive.
- Renderer, validator, package, or generated-artifact risk: None. The importer produces standard architecture IR that passes the existing schema and layout validation.
- Failure behavior: Unsupported, ambiguous, or malformed syntax exits non-zero with a stable named diagnostic. Open links (`---` / long-arrow forms), subgraph `direction` directives, empty/whitespace labels, and XML 1.0-disallowed characters are explicitly rejected. No node or edge is silently discarded.

## Tests run (head `d5f99c90`, synced onto `dev` @ `96234021`, post-v3.1.0)

```bash
node --test test/flowchart-import.test.mjs
```

Result: **96 tests, 96 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped** on `d5f99c90` (includes the operator-family cases; `cli`, `cli-output-types`, and `output-path` surfaces are covered by the full suite below).

```bash
npm test
```

Result (full suite, `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`, on `d5f99c90` = dev-sync merge of `96234021` plus the receipt-drain fix): **3,234 tests, 3,115 pass, 2 fail, 117 skipped**. The +665 test delta vs the prior run is upstream's v3.1.0 suite growth; skips remain browser/Chrome-gated tests on this environment. The 2 failures are pre-existing on `dev` tip `96234021` and reproduce on a clean `origin/dev` worktree — stale checked-in artifacts, not this change: `test/gallery.test.mjs` (regenerate via `scripts/build-gallery.mjs`) and `test/architecture-delta.test.mjs` "checked-in Checkout compare artifact is reproducible from its authoritative inputs". Duration: ~410 s.

```bash
npm run check:release-identity
```

Result: fails identically on clean `origin/dev` `96234021` — `scripts/{start,guide,gallery}-template.html` carry a hardcoded version instead of `[[ARCHIFY_VERSION]]` in upstream's mid-release dev state; unrelated to this change.

```bash
ARCHIFY_CHROME=/home/ubuntu/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux-arm64/chrome \
  ARCHIFY_CHROME_NO_SANDBOX=1 \
  node bin/archify.mjs visual-check <delivered>.html --json
```

Result: automated browser containment, readability, and viewer-chrome checks pass on the delivered flowchart HTML across 1440×900, 1600×1000, 1920×1080, and 2048×1320 viewports (see Visual evidence).

End-to-end `import flowchart` → `validate architecture --quality showcase` → `deliver architecture --quality showcase` → `visual-check` was verified on the representative `valid-labeled-subgraph.mmd` and `valid-long-labels.mmd` fixtures.

## Visual evidence

Perceptual visual review: passed.

A representative Mermaid flowchart with a subgraph (`Edge`) and directed, labeled edges was imported, validated at showcase quality, delivered, and inspected in a real headless Chromium instance:

```bash
node archify/bin/archify.mjs import flowchart test/fixtures/flowchart/valid-labeled-subgraph.mmd labeled-subgraph.json --json
node archify/bin/archify.mjs validate architecture labeled-subgraph.json --quality showcase --json
node archify/bin/archify.mjs deliver architecture labeled-subgraph.json labeled-subgraph.html --quality showcase --json
ARCHIFY_CHROME=/path/to/chrome ARCHIFY_CHROME_NO_SANDBOX=1 node archify/bin/archify.mjs visual-check labeled-subgraph.html --json
```

A second fixture with a long component label inside a `Platform` boundary was also imported, validated, delivered, and visual-checked:

```bash
node archify/bin/archify.mjs import flowchart test/fixtures/flowchart/valid-long-labels.mmd long-labels.json --json
node archify/bin/archify.mjs validate architecture long-labels.json --quality showcase --json
node archify/bin/archify.mjs deliver architecture long-labels.json long-labels.html --quality showcase --json
ARCHIFY_CHROME=/path/to/chrome ARCHIFY_CHROME_NO_SANDBOX=1 node archify/bin/archify.mjs visual-check long-labels.html --json
```

Both delivered HTMLs pass `visual-check` containment, readability, and viewer-chrome checks on all inspected viewports. The rendered diagrams show the boundary group, readable labels, correct left-to-right layout, and the toolbar/preset UI.

## Generated artifacts

`archify.zip` was rebuilt twice with Node 22 (`v22.23.2`, bundled zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`) producing byte-identical output (`sha256:7ea6f682…`) after merging current `tt-a1i/dev` (`96234021`, post-v3.1.0) into the feature branch; provenance vs upstream's zip is exactly the two added files (`archify/importers/flowchart.mjs`, `archify/references/mermaid-flowchart-import.md`). No other generated artifacts were touched.

## Checklist

- [x] I used a minimal focused change and preserved existing typed JSON behavior unless the issue requires a contract change.
- [x] I ran the relevant targeted tests and `npm test` in `archify/`.
- [x] I added or updated a regression test for behavioral changes.
- [x] I checked generated artifacts and package freshness when their sources changed.
- [x] I removed secrets, private repository content, and customer data from fixtures and screenshots.

Closes #92

items.title: feat(erd): add entity-relationship diagrams (consolidated onto dev, reading round applied)
items.body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

`dev` has no type for the shape of the data itself. A `database`-typed architecture node names a store, but not a key, a foreign-key target, or whether an end is one or many, so "map this service's data model" can only be approximated. This implements #115: `erd` becomes a sixth typed diagram — entities, key attributes, and both-end cardinality — authored as JSON, validated fail-closed, and delivered as a self-contained HTML artifact that reuses the existing viewer.

## The larger example now fits a laptop viewport

The review asked for the diagram itself to be complete and readable inside the laptop viewport without scrolling, and said that shrinking text or dropping model information would not meet that goal. Both are true of this arrangement: nothing is dropped, and the text gets **larger**.

[`examples/subscription-billing.erd.json`](archify/examples/subscription-billing.erd.json) — eleven tables, sixty-four fields, four domains — is now authored one domain per column instead of one per row. Measured at 1440×900, same tables and same typography:

| | canvas | rendered | scale | field types |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| one domain per row | 910×874 | 777px | 0.85 | 9.0px |
| one domain per column | 1230×678 | **1346px** | 1.09 | **11.5px** |

Both are contained with no scroll; the wide arrangement is rendered at the full reader width instead of being narrowed to fit the height, which is where the three extra pixels come from. The reason a horizontal arrangement cannot simply be widened instead: the reader scales a canvas whose ratio is at least 1.55 up to the reader width, so extra columns cost text size rather than buying it.

The honest limit: the binding constraint is the reader's height budget. This model lands at 11.5px with about 12px of slack in the page; a model half again as tall — roughly sixteen tables at this field density — would either be narrowed below the readable floor or start to scroll. The lever I would pull next is a second view for the overview, not smaller type. That is the tradeoff to discuss with real examples.

## The table header and the domain bands (head `791abcd9`)

This answers the question in the `c3db4c9`/`875c72f` review about the header text. Rather than measure the note, we removed it: the header carries one string, the table title, centered on the table's own center line and held inside the interval it is measured against. `erd/header-text-capacity` now covers the title alone, so its fixes no longer mention a second header line, and the header note's measurement path and the two layout constants that sized it are gone.

The band is the only place a domain name is drawn, so removing the note meant the band rules had to carry that weight instead of losing it:

- A one-table domain is a band. It used to fall back to the header note, and that fallback no longer exists.
- "One row with adjacent columns, or one column with adjacent rows" became "the members fill a solid block of grid cells". A block is the same claim with both dimensions, and the band it draws encloses no cell the domain does not own; an L-shape or a row with a gap is still refused.
- A tag that cannot be banded is refused with `erd/domain-not-drawn` rather than published with its tables complete and its domain unnamed. Refusal covers members that do not fill one block, a member placed outside the grid (a table carrying `pos` is drawn there, not at its cells), a band whose padding would cover an unrelated table because `layout.gapX`/`gapY` are smaller than the padding, and a caption the canvas does not reach. Two members in one cell stay the grid placement check's report, so the author gets the pair that has to move rather than a block to rebuild.

Your point that silently dropping authored content is the wrong failure is the one we took: the note is removed by design rather than dropped by measurement, and what is left is a render that refuses to draw a domain it cannot name.

## Automated-review fixes (head `d948e696`)

Two contract gaps the automated review found at `5da9afcc`, both fixed at the source rather than at the drawing:

**`variant` could outrank `identifying: false`.** `{ "identifying": false, "variant": "emphasis" }` was drawn solid, which contradicts the documented convention that a non-identifying relationship is dashed. `identifying: false` now owns the dash, and the schema *rejects* the contradiction instead of resolving it silently — the solid variants and the dash state opposite facts, and dropping either one is worse than refusing the pair. `validate erd --json` reports it at `/relationships/<n>/variant` with the relationship id, `variant: "dashed"` remains accepted as the same drawing, and a `variant` on an identifying relationship still selects the accent. `markerStyleOf()` keeps the precedence in the renderer too, so a document that never passed the schema cannot paint a non-identifying relationship solid.

**A column could not be both the primary and a foreign key.** `key` now takes one role or a list — `{ "name": "tenant_id", "type": "bigint", "key": ["pk", "fk"], "references": "tenant.id" }` — which is the junction-table shape. Each role draws its own marker in its legend's ink, in the order the author declared them; a role named twice draws once. The key column is measured from the widest run in the table, never narrower than the shared 30-unit column, so tables stating a single role keep the exact bytes they had, and the field-name budget is charged that width so a three-marker run cannot run into the name. A list is validated exactly like a single role: every `fk` in it still requires `references`, and the target is still checked against the declared entities and attributes.

Neither example carries a composite key, so all four rendered ERD HTML files are byte-identical to this head's parent, and the reading evidence below still applies unchanged.

## Design decisions worth naming

- A column states every key role it carries: `key` is a role or a list, so a junction column is `["pk", "fk"]` rather than one fact hiding the other, and the schema rejects a list that repeats or invents a role.
- Cardinality is typed, not display notation: `fromCardinality`/`toCardinality` are `one`/`many` and required at both ends, so nothing about an end is inferred from the other end or parsed from a display string.
- No authored `kind`: `junction` and `external` are derivable from the key facts, so an authored enum could contradict the keys the same document declares.
- No attribute-count cap: the real constraint is box height and single-line fit, so a row that cannot fit is a diagnostic instead of a silently truncated cell.
- Entity boxes are opaque: a route that would pass through an unrelated entity is routed around it, and an unroutable relationship is an error rather than a drawn crossing.
- A table side holds only so many ends: the port spread is a cap, so an over-subscribed side is `layout/marker-capacity` rather than overlapping glyphs.
- The crow's foot opens toward the entity it describes, and the legend repeats the glyph the diagram draws. #183's orphan/`standalone` policy remains a deliberate scope choice, not an omission: say the word and I will take it as a separate change.
